concept: Apple NVMe small random read latency under F_NOCACHE at queue depth 16
summary: Existing benchmarks that skip F_NOCACHE can serve reads from the unified buffer cache, so results vary with installed RAM (author's claim; a forum reply disputes it on the basis that SATA and HDD speeds looked like device speeds).

facts.text: Existing benchmarks that skip F_NOCACHE can serve reads from the unified buffer cache, so results vary with installed RAM (author's claim; a forum reply disputes it on the basis that SATA and HDD speeds looked like device speeds).

DiskTruth author: BlackMagic and AmorphousDiskMark do not use F_NOCACHE and are inflated by RAM caching on large-memory Macs. A MacRumors reply (bzgnyc2/!!!) says those tools gave device-consistent speeds on SATA SSD (<500 MB/s) and HDD (~200 MB/s), so caching is not evident. Shown side by side, not resolved.
DiskTruth (beta announced 2026-04-16) sets fcntl(fd, F_NOCACHE, 1) on every file descriptor before any I/O.
DiskTruth measures random 4K IOPS and latency at QD1 with 10,000 operations per pass and reports average and p99.
DiskTruth measures queue-depth scaling at QD1, QD4, QD16 and QD32 with 3,000 ops per level.
Its author states Apple Silicon internal NVMe has "extraordinary QD1 latency" and less dramatic scaling at higher depths than desktop NVMe, with no numbers given in the post.
DiskTruth uses a 16 GB test file, 3 iterations and the median for sequential tests.
The ds4 QD16 stall estimate remains incomplete: no measured latency number exists in the sources read.
